extracted.intended_audience: home cooks / domestic cooks (historical cookbook readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, prescriptive instructions for preparing sauces, vegetables, puddings, and related cookery; aimed at household cooks preparing 19th‑century domestic meals. Focuses on selection, preparation, cooking times, and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingredient freshness and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use fresh, properly chosen ingredients: eggs must be fresh; peas must be quite young and gathered early in the morning; choose cauliflowers that are 'close and white' and of middle size; purple eggplants are best; select sweet potatoes of roughly the same size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and repeated notes: 'Eggs must be fresh, or they will not heal well.' 'To have them in perfection, they must be quite young, gathered early in the morning...' Use the varietal/ripeness guidance given for each vegetable to preserve delicate flavour and texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match sizes for even cooking
rubrics_metrics.description: When boiling or roasting (especially potatoes and sweet potatoes), choose pieces of equal size so they will be done equally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For potatos: 'fill a sauce-pan half full of potatos of equal size, (or make them so by dividing the large ones.)' For sweet potatoes: 'Take those that are nearly of the same size, that they may be done equally.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Control water quantity when boiling
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust the amount of water for the item: potatoes should be merely covered (about an inch), not drowned; many vegetables require plenty of boiling water; some items benefit from two waters to remove harshness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warnings: 'most boiled things are spoiled by having too little water, but potatos are often spoiled by having too much' and for strong old cabbages 'it will much ameliorate the flavour... to boil them in two waters.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Test doneness with a fork / sensory checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a fork to test tenderness; do not rely on skin‑cracking as an indicator (especially for potatoes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit guidance: 'The best way to try if they are done enough, is to pierce them with a fork.' and 'place no dependence on the usual test of their skin's cracking... which... may happen when they are not half done.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overcooking — timing is critical
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove vegetables at the instant they become tender to preserve flavor and color; a minute or two more can spoil them (e.g., asparagus, cauliflower).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: asparagus 'when they are tender at the stalk, which will be in from twenty to thirty minutes, they are done enough. Great care must be taken to watch the exact time...' and cauliflower 'take it up the moment it is enough: a few minutes longer boiling will spoil it.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful washing, picking and draining
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoroughly pick and wash greens and vegetables, drain them well before cooking or serving to remove grit and excess water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: 'The lettuce, pepper grass, chervil, cress, &c. should be... nicely picked, washed, and laid in cold water, which will be improved by adding ice.' 'Wash and pare a large bunch of celery very clean... drain perfectly dry.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Parboiling and blanching to remove bitterness or skins
rubrics_metrics.description: Use parboiling or blanching to remove bitter tastes or skins (e.g., parboil eggplant to take off bitter taste; blanch almonds to slip skins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The purple [eggplants]... get them young and fresh; pull out the stem, and parboil them to take off the bitter taste.' 'Almonds should be put in hot water till the skins will slip off, which is called blanching.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Pan and fat cleanliness for frying
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure frying pan and fat are clean before frying to avoid off-flavors and poor texture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit warning: 'Take care that your fat and frying-pan are quite clean; put it on a quick fire...' for frying sliced potatoes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frying technique: heat, spacing, and motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat fat until it boils and is still before adding items; add items carefully and keep them moving until crisp; drain on a sieve and season lightly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure for sliced potatoes: 'as soon as the lard boils and is still, put in the slices of potatos, and keep moving them till they are crisp; take them up, and lay them to drain on a sieve; send them up with very little salt sprinkled on them.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Drain and dry before mashing or finishing
rubrics_metrics.description: After boiling, drain and dry items well before mashing or putting into dishes to avoid watery results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'When the potatos are thoroughly boiled, drain and dry them perfectly' (for mashing) and after boiling vegetables 'lay them on a sieve till the water is thoroughly drained from them.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Mashing technique and proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rub boiled vegetables (potatoes, turnips) through a colander before finishing; add measured butter and milk and do not make too moist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For mashed potatoes: 'to a pound of potatos put half an ounce of butter, and a table-spoonful of milk; do not make them too moist; mix them well together.' For purees and turnips similar rubbing/straining instructions are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve sauces separately when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not always pour sauces over the main item; serve delicate melted butter or other sauces in a boat so guests may add as desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Do not pour butter over them, but send some in a boat.' for asparagus; melted butter 'should be sent in a boat' with artichokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melting butter (double-boiler method) to avoid oiling
rubrics_metrics.description: Melt butter in a small covered pan set into a larger pan of boiling water, with flour and a little water mixed in; shake constantly until melted and boiling. Do not set the butter pan directly on coals or it will oil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full method: 'Keep a quart tin sauce-pan, with a cover to it, exclusively for this purpose; weigh one quarter of a pound of good butter; rub into it two tea-spoonsful of flour; ... put the sauce-pan in a larger one of boiling water; shake it constantly till completely melted, and beginning to boil. If the pan containing the butter be set on coals, it will oil the butter and spoil it.' Add two spoonsful of water when herbs are added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent butter from oiling in sauces
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid overheating or direct heat when making butter-based sauces and take care with quantities of water when herbs are added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Take care the butter does not oil.' and 'When herbs are added to butter, you must put two spoonsful of water instead of one.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate thickeners and techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Thicken sauces with butter rolled in flour, egg yolks and cream, or brown flour and butter as applicable; keep stirring when using egg yolks to prevent curdling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: oyster sauce thickened 'with butter rolled in flour'; mushroom sauce adds 'half a pint of cream, and the yelks of two eggs beat very well--keep stirring it till it boils up.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Herbs: preparation and infusion care
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare herbs carefully (boil parsley 10 minutes, pick leaves, dry and mince); infuse herb flavors by repeated short infusions to avoid extracting coarse/bitter tastes; do not allow herb infusions to stand too long (thyme/mint >20 hours produces bitterness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods: parsley 'boil them ten minutes in salt and water, drain them perfectly dry, mince them exceedingly fine' and thyme infusion: 'gathering it when in full perfection... put a large handful... pour on a quart of vinegar or brandy... next day, take all the thyme out, put in as much more; do this a third time...' Warning: 'if permitted to stand more than twenty hours in the liquor they are infused in, a coarse and bitter taste will be extracted, particularly from mint.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and pickling procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for preserving and pickling: make celery vinegar by pounding seed, filling with strong vinegar and shaking daily for a fortnight; preserve beans in salted kegs with weight; for thyme infusion repeat short infusions rather than long maceration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stepwise instructions and timing: 'Pound two gills of celery seed, put it into a bottle and fill it with strong vinegar; shake it every day for a fortnight, then strain it.' Bean preserving: 'sprinkle some salt in the bottom, put in a layer of pods... lay a board on with a weight... keep it in a dry, cool place.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Puff paste technique: butter incorporation and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a stiff paste, roll and incorporate cold butter in portions, folding and rolling until butter is mingled; handle lightly with hands; bake in a moderate oven that allows rising without browning; good paste looks 'white, and as light as a feather.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed steps: sift flour, make stiff paste with cold water, divide butter into four parts, put butter in little bits, fold and roll repeatedly, touch lightly with hands, bake in moderate oven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bake and pudding readiness and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Have every ingredient ready and the oven/moulds prepared before beginning puddings or cakes; promptness at stages is necessary to avoid injury to the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Before a pudding or cake is begun, every ingredient necessary for it must be ready; when the process is retarded by neglecting to have them prepared, the article is injured. The oven must be in a proper state... Promptitude is necessary...'

rubrics_metrics.name: Egg handling in baking and custards
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate yolks and whites (preferable though more trouble); beat eggs to make them light before use; when mixing eggs into hot milk, cool the milk or set it on the fire only a few minutes and stir constantly to avoid poaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'It is better to separate the yelks from the whites always... eggs injure every thing, unless they are made light before they are used.' 'When they are to be mixed with milk, let it cool after boiling, or the eggs will poach; and only set it on the fire a few minutes... stirring it all the time.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Salt handling in sweet baking and greasing moulds
rubrics_metrics.description: Wash salt from butter that is to be used with sugar or to grease moulds for baking, to avoid a disagreeable salt taste on baked articles' outer side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'The salt should always be washed from butter, when it is to be used in any thing that has sugar for an ingredient, and also from that which is melted to grease any kind of mould for baking--otherwise, there will be a disagreeable salt taste on the outer side of the article baked.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare dried fruits and nuts before use
rubrics_metrics.description: Stone and halve raisins, dust them with flour to prevent clumping; wash and dry currants thoroughly; blanch almonds and pound them with rose/orange flower water to avoid oiling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Raisins should be stoned and cut in two, and have some flour sifted over them... Currants require washing in many waters to cleanse them; they must be picked and well dried... Almonds should be put in hot water till the skins will slip off... They must always be pounded with rose or orange flower water, to prevent their oiling.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification technique for jellies (animal gelatin jellies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make jelly by boiling feet or similar, strain, chill and remove grease, mix with wine, lemon, sugar and spices; clarify by adding whipped egg whites and crushed shells, heat until clear on one side and dross accumulates on the other, skim, then leach through a bag until transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed process: 'Boil four calfs' feet... strain the liquor... when cold, take all the grease off... add wine, lemon juice, sugar, cinnamon and mace... whip up the whites to a froth, crush the shells and put with them, mix it with the jelly, set it on the fire, stir it occasionally till the jelly is melted, but do not touch it afterwards. When it has boiled till it looks quite clear on one side, and the dross accumulates on the other, take off carefully the thickest part of the dross, and pour the jelly in the bag; put back what runs through, until it becomes quite transparent.' Keep covered to avoid dust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forcemeat preparation and cooking options
rubrics_metrics.description: Make forcemeat (veal + suet + herbs + spices + egg yolks), shape into balls or long pieces, roll in flour and fry until brown; if for white sauce, boil them in hot water instead of frying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipe and usage: 'Take half a pound of veal, and half a pound of suet cut fine... add... the yelks of two eggs; mix them well together, and make them into balls... then roll them in flour, and fry them brown. If they are for the use of white sauce, do not fry them, but put them in a sauce-pan of hot water and let them boil a few minutes.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Rice washing and cooking proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Wash rice in several waters until water is clear; use two and a half cups of cold water to every two cups (or per recipe proportion), add a teaspoon salt, boil ten minutes, pour off most water, then let rice soak/dry over coals about fifteen minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Put two cups full of rice in a bowl of water, rub it well... pour off the water; do this until the water ceases to be discoloured; then put the rice into two and a half cups of cold water; add a tea-spoonful of salt, cover the pot close, and set it on a brisk fire; let it boil ten minutes, pour off the greater part of the water, and remove the pot to a bed of coals, where it must remain a quarter of an hour to soak and dry.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Mushroom selection and cooking
rubrics_metrics.description: Select grown mushrooms that are still young enough to have red gills; wash and remove the top skin of the cap; stew without additional water, seasoning lightly and thickening with butter and brown flour; red wine optional but often unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Gather grown mushrooms, but such as are young enough to have red gills; cut off that part of the stem which grew in the earth--wash them carefully, and take the skin from the top; put them into a stew pan with some salt, but no water--stew them till tender, and thicken them with a spoonful of butter, mixed with one of brown flour; red wine may be added, but the flavour of the mushroom is too delicious to require aid from any thing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect vegetable-specific cooking times and tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the specified approximate timing and tests for each vegetable (e.g., asparagus 20–30 minutes, small cauliflower 15 minutes, large 20 minutes; artichokes 1.5–2 hours; parsnips 1–2 hours depending on size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly gives per-item timings and emphasizes testing by tenderness: 'A young cabbage will take about twenty minutes, or half an hour; when full grown, nearly an hour.' 'Artichokes... will take an hour and a half, or two hours' etc. Use fork tests and visual signs given for each vegetable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and garnishing practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use garnishes and serving aids (toast under asparagus, melted butter in cups, forcemeat balls for ragouts, bacon center for Mazagan beans) to enhance appearance and flavor; arrange attractively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'toast a slice of a loaf... dip it lightly in the liquor the asparagus was boiled in, and lay it in the middle of a dish... pour some melted butter on the toast, and lay the asparagus upon it.' 'Put a small bit of middling... cover it with bread crumbs, and toast it; lay this in the middle of the dish' for beans.
